Project 02 / Lux NetworkExplore the project ↘
OverviewIterationsSolutionDesign system
01 / Overview

A faster path from decision to trade.

Lux Network is a crypto-native financial infrastructure platform with DeFi tools including a native DEX, orderbook trading, and multi-chain asset management. As it expanded into traditional derivatives markets, order placement needed to serve more demanding traders.

The problem

Prices could change every 0.3 seconds. The existing flow made order placement slower and frustrated high-frequency traders.

My approach

I reviewed the entire flow, removed non-critical steps, and refined how screens transitioned into one another.

Starting point4.8s

Earlier Lux Network order time.

02 / Existing flow

Too many moments between intent and action.

The status screen alone took about 1.2 seconds. The move from buy or sell to the order card added three transitions.

03 / Iterations

Finding the lightest change that worked.

Redesigning the order card across the ecosystem would have been a large technical effort, so I explored ways to improve speed without rebuilding that shared component.

01Explored

Order card as a new panel

This is the shared order card the concept would change. I explored placing it in a smaller panel, but the card also served asset transfers across the ecosystem, making a redesign a large engineering effort.

02Explored

A full-screen confirmation remained

This version still ended on a status screen after the buy order. That pause became the next part of the flow to remove.

03Selected

Bottom sheet → order card

The selected approach scaled the sheet directly into the full-screen card, removing an extra transition.

04 / The solution

Keep the trader moving.

The shipped flow replaced the status screen with a toast and streamlined the move into the order card.

1.2sSaved by removing the status screen
0.6sSaved by streamlining transitions
40%Faster shipped flow
05 / Key decisions

Two changes. One faster flow.

01

Status screen → status toast

The status screen became a toast, so traders landed directly on the positions page after buying. The toast still needed to communicate every state the screen had handled.

−1.2s
02

Three transitions → one

The bottom sheet scaled directly into the full-screen order card. We used quick cubic ease-out and ease-in motion to keep the interaction responsive.

−0.6s
06 / Shipping to the system

A reusable status pattern.

The status toast was carried into the design system with states, light and dark modes, and placement guidance.
